A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Primitive Prompt Learning (PPL) study, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures and tables. Both end with references; neither contains the appendix mentioned in Section 5.2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MimicGen/LIBERO simulation and Franka Panda experiments, including success rates, lifelong learning comparisons, ablations and lighting robustness tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5, Tables 1–3 and Figures 6–9.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same two-stage PPL procedure, motion-aware querying and prompt expansion. Changing 'appended' to 'concatenated' in the abstract describes the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MimicGen/LIBERO-derived skill data and Franka Panda manipulation tasks, including the same static and changing lighting scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 7 retain the same comparator membership, including Sequential, ER, LoRA, Diffusion-Transformer and MOE in their corresponding experiments. The newly cited LOTUS work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same demonstration counts, experimental setup and FWT/BWT evaluation procedures. No evaluation protocol or experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The text-only versus text-flow query analysis, prompt-count study, pretrained-prompt ablations and lighting robustness tests remain unchanged in Section 5.4, Figures 6 and 8–9, and Table 3.

E5.justification: Both versions report 15 independent runs per real-world skill and retain the same uncertainty reporting in Tables 1–2 and Figure 7. No new statistical estimation or testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and Figure 7, the plotted ablation results, and the reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same average PPL FWT of 0.83 ± 0.03.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations (1)–(11), brightness-constancy assumption and mathematical description of PPL are unchanged. No formal result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about reusable primitives, lifelong knowledge transfer, the constructed skill dataset and superior performance. The abstract's prompt wording does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of shared primitives, prompt-count tradeoffs and training efficiency remain unchanged. Both versions discuss the same lighting-related weakness and propose depth information and 3D scene flow as future work.

D1.justification: The disclosed model components, demonstration counts and robot platform are unchanged. No implementation details, hyperparameters, computing-resource information or code/data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a citation to LOTUS: Continual Imitation Learning for Robot Manipulation through Unsupervised Skill Discovery, with a new reference entry. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged; the SpatialVLA and MaxMI edits update existing bibliographic records.

P1.justification: The abstract changes 'lifelong prompts are appended' to 'new prompts are concatenated.' Acknowledgements are shortened and bibliographic details are edited, while the section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–3 retain their displays and placement. The shortened acknowledgements and reference edits produce limited reflow on pages 9–11, alongside minor text wrapping and changes to the arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: The LOTUS citation and bibliographic updates provide small attribution benefits, while the abstract edit is essentially equivalent wording. These limited edits leave the paper's clarity, experimental support, reproducibility and limitations materially unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
